transcript.text: lg w/d keeps saying dE n wont start?? door is shut

I can’t confirm exactly what “dE” means on this particular LG washer-dryer without its model-specific code information, but with the door shut and the machine refusing to start, it points most strongly to the door not being recognised as safely closed. That can be a worn/misaligned catch or hinge, a failed electrical door interlock, or less commonly a control/child-lock setting. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Open the door and check the rubber seal and latch area for trapped clothing, a coin or detergent residue. Check that the small hook on the door is not bent or loose, and that the door sits square rather than drooping. Close it firmly until it clicks. A door that only works when lifted/pushed usually indicates alignment, hinge or catch wear. 2. Check whether a padlock/key symbol is lit. If so, cancel the child lock using the button combination shown on the control panel/manual, then retry. 3. With the door closed, press Start and listen/feel for a lock click. If there is no locking click and the error returns straight away despite the door closing cleanly, the electrical door interlock is the leading suspect. Do not force the door or try to bypass the lock. If the door looks sound but there is no lock click, an engineer is normally the sensible next step: the interlock and its wiring need testing with the appliance isolated before any part is fitted.

ok did the unplug thing n checked. theres a king size duvet in there bulging against the glass n a corner is squashed in the seal. door closes but springs back a bit. just a click then nothing when i press start

The duvet caught in the seal is the most likely reason for the dE/start refusal. The door needs to sit fully home against the seal so the latch and electrical lock can engage; if it springs back, it is not properly shut even though it looks closed. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Remove the duvet completely — do not force the door against it.
2. Check the whole seal lip is free of fabric, then close the empty door. It should stay closed rather than springing back.
3. Plug it back in and try a short rinse programme. A single click followed by normal starting means the obstruction was the cause. A king-size duvet may also be too bulky for the drum even if it does fit; it can prevent reliable door closure and later cause an out-of-balance spin. If the empty door now closes properly but it still gives dE after the click, the likely next cause is the door interlock or its connection, which needs an engineer to test with the appliance isolated. Do not try to bypass the lock.
ok took the duvet out n tried towels, starts fine. so its just the duvet being too big?

Yes — in this case the duvet was too bulky in the drum and was stopping the door from seating fully against the seal. The fact it starts normally with towels rules out the door lock as the current problem. For a king-size duvet, use a larger-capacity machine or a laundrette/commercial washer if possible. Even if it can be made to fit, it can trap in the seal again and, once wet, may be too heavy and uneven for the machine to spin safely. No repair is needed if it continues to start normally with ordinary loads.

candidates: Door interlock not recognising the closed door (high)
Door catch, hinge alignment or trapped laundry preventing proper engagement (medium)

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
